Site.faq1A: SciSpark is an AI research workspace for discovering papers, reading with context, and building connected knowledge. It brings your paper feed, personal wiki, knowledge graph, and research ideas into one place, with Sparky as your research companion.
Site.faq2Q: How is the hosted version different from local?
Site.faq2A: The hosted beta runs in your browser and keeps your vault online. Local installation stores your Markdown vault on your computer. Both approaches may send requests to scholarly services and your chosen AI provider. Automatic sync between hosted and local vaults is not currently part of this offer.
Site.faq3Q: Do I need my own AI API key?
Site.faq3A: The hosted beta includes a starter AI allowance, and you can choose to connect your own API key. Local installation needs an API provider or a signed-in Codex or Claude Code CLI for AI features. Provider charges depend on the option you use.
Site.faq4A: SciSpark uses your research interests and profile to guide paper discovery. In the preview above, choose one of three prepared topics to see an example of how discovery connects to reading, notes, and ideas. The preview is not a live recommendation feed.
Site.faq5A: A native mobile app is planned, so your research can be closer at hand. For now, you can open the hosted beta in your browser.
Site.closingBody: Discover with purpose. Read with context. Keep what you learn.
Site.footerLine: One workspace, from discovery to your next experiment.
Site.fallback: The interactive preview could not load. You can still explore SciSpark in the beta.

Topics.aiWhy: Connects your interest in language models with how information is represented and retrieved.
Topics.aiNote: Attention helps a model relate parts of an input. Retrieval brings external information into generation. Together, they open questions about context and evidence.
Topics.aiQuestion: When does retrieving a source help more than adding a longer context?
Topics.aiMethod: Compare the two approaches on the same questions, checking source attribution as well as answer quality.
Topics.climateWhy: Connects your interest in climate and energy with methods for modeling a changing atmosphere.
Topics.climateNote: Graph-based and transformer-based models offer different ways to represent weather. Comparing their assumptions can inform questions about forecasts and extreme events.
Topics.climateQuestion: How do learned weather models behave when the conditions become unusual?
Topics.climateMethod: Compare forecast errors across ordinary conditions and selected extremes, using the same regions, dates, and evaluation targets.
Topics.mindWhy: Connects your interest in learning and behavior with models of how people understand the world and other minds.
Topics.mindNote: Causal understanding and models of other agents offer complementary perspectives on learning. Observed behavior can inspire hypotheses, without establishing a model of human cognition.
Topics.mindQuestion: What kind of prior knowledge helps a learner infer another agent's goals?
Topics.mindMethod: Compare learners with different prior knowledge on the same observed behaviors, keeping computational results separate from claims about people.

Papers.attentionSummary: The Transformer uses attention to connect information across a sequence, without recurrent or convolutional layers. The paper evaluates the architecture on translation tasks.
Papers.ragTitle: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
Papers.ragSummary: RAG combines a generative model with retrieved passages, bringing external sources into knowledge-intensive language tasks.
Papers.graphcastTitle: GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
Papers.graphcastSummary: GraphCast learns from weather reanalysis data and uses a graph neural network to predict the evolution of atmospheric conditions.
Papers.panguTitle: Pangu-Weather: A 3D High-Resolution Model for Fast and Accurate Global Weather Forecast
Papers.panguSummary: Pangu-Weather uses a three-dimensional transformer and temporal aggregation to model global weather from historical atmospheric data.
Papers.learningTitle: Building Machines That Learn and Think Like People
Papers.learningSummary: This perspective connects cognitive science and machine learning, emphasizing causal models, compositionality, and learning from limited experience.
Papers.mindSummary: A neural network learns to predict agents' behavior from observations in simplified environments. The study explores computational models of other agents.
